summary: Clarifies BGP origin validation based on RPKI. Deployment has been hampered by vendor misimplementations about which routes are validated and whether policy is applied when not configured, and this document explains the intended behavior.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8481 clarifies that routers evaluate all BGP routes for RPKI origin validation unless an operator configures otherwise. It also says routers must not apply policy based on the result without explicit operator configuration; RFC 9324 later updated this memo.

questions: how does bgp origin validation work
what does rpki validation state mean
how should routers handle invalid routes
subtitle: Clarifies which BGP routes receive RPKI origin-validation states and who controls policy.

tldr.problem: Implementations differed on which routes receive RPKI origin validation and whether they apply policy without operator configuration.
tldr.mechanism: Routers must evaluate and set a validation state for all BGP routes from any source unless configured otherwise, and must not apply policy without operator configuration.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8481 updates RFC 6811 and is updated by RFC 9324.

today: RFC 8481 is updated by RFC 9324. It updates RFC 6811.

sections.title: Two Sources of Implementation Differences
sections.content:
RPKI-based BGP origin validation assigns each route a state: NotFound, Valid, or Invalid. The RFC says deployment was hampered by differences in which routes implementations evaluated and whether they applied policy when the operator had not configured it.

This memo updates RFC 6811 to clarify those two points. It does not change how a router determines the validation state.
sections.plainLanguage: The problem was not how routers decide a route's validation state. The problem was which routes they checked and whether they acted on the result automatically.

sections.title: Evaluate Every BGP Route
sections.content:
A router must evaluate and set the validation state of all routes in BGP from any source, including eBGP, iBGP, and routes redistributed from static or connected sources, unless the operator specifically configures otherwise.

When a route is redistributed into BGP, the input has no AS_PATH from which to validate the originating Autonomous System. The router must use the AS number from its BGP configuration. If that is ambiguous because of a confederation, migration, or other multi-AS configuration, the router configuration must provide a way to specify the AS to use.
sections.plainLanguage: Check every route that enters BGP, regardless of its source, unless the operator changes that behavior. For redistributed routes, the router uses a configured AS number for validation.

sections.title: Set the State and Let the Operator Choose
sections.content:
After a route receives a validation state, the operator controls any policy based on that state. Policy must not be applied without specific operator configuration. Automatic origin-validation actions, including those described in RFC 8097, must not occur unless the operator configures them.

The RFC says it creates no security considerations beyond those of RFC 6811 and has no IANA actions.
sections.plainLanguage: The router records whether a route is Valid, Invalid, or NotFound. The operator decides what policy to apply; the router must not make that choice on its own.
